questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are acute angles such that $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha-\beta$ satisfy the equation $\tan^2\theta-4\tan\theta+1=0$, then $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are respectively
questions.explanation: Product of roots $=1 \Rightarrow \tan(\alpha+\beta)\tan(\alpha-\beta)=1 \Rightarrow (\alpha+\beta)+(\alpha-\beta)=90^\circ \Rightarrow \alpha=45^\circ$. Sum of roots $=4$ then gives $\tan\beta=1/\sqrt3 \Rightarrow \beta=30^\circ$.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\sin(x+\pi/6)+\cos(x+\pi/6)$ is attained at $x=$
questions.explanation: $\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\sqrt2\sin(\theta+\pi/4)$ is maximum when $\theta+\pi/4=\pi/2$, i.e. $x+\pi/6+\pi/4=\pi/2\Rightarrow x=\pi/12$.

questions.q: The angles of a triangle are in A.P and the greatest angle is double the least angle, then sine of the third angle is
questions.explanation: Let angles be $a-d,a,a+d$; sum gives $a=60^\circ$. Greatest $=$ twice least: $a+d=2(a-d)\Rightarrow d=20^\circ$. The angles are $40^\circ,60^\circ,80^\circ$; the third (middle) angle is $60^\circ$, and $\sin60^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

questions.q: Which of the following is not correct?
questions.explanation: $\cos5\pi=-1$ while $\cos4\pi=1$, so they are not equal; all other options hold true.

questions.q: If $\cos x + \cos^2 x = 1$, then the value of $\sin^2 x + \sin^4 x$ is
questions.explanation: From $\cos x = \sin^2 x$, substitute: $\sin^2x+\sin^4x=\cos x+\cos^2x=1$.

questions.q: If in two circles, arcs of the same length subtend angles $30^0$ and $78^0$ at the centre, then the ratio of their radii is
questions.explanation: Equal arc length gives $r_1\theta_1=r_2\theta_2$, so $\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}=\dfrac{\theta_2}{\theta_1}=\dfrac{78}{30}=\dfrac{13}{5}$.

questions.q: If $\triangle ABC$ is right angled at $C$, then the value of $\tan A+\tan B$ is
questions.explanation: With the right angle at $C$, $\tan A=\dfrac{a}{b}$ and $\tan B=\dfrac{b}{a}$, so $\tan A+\tan B=\dfrac{a^2+b^2}{ab}=\dfrac{c^2}{ab}$ by Pythagoras.

questions.q: The value of $e^{\log_{10}\tan1° + \log_{10}\tan2° + \log_{10}\tan3° + \cdots + \log_{10}\tan89°}$ is
questions.explanation: The sum of logs equals $\log_{10}(\tan1°\tan2°\cdots\tan89°) = \log_{10}1 = 0$ (pairing $\tan\theta\cdot\tan(90°-\theta)=1$), so $e^0=1$.

questions.q: The value of $\begin{vmatrix}\sin^2 14° & \sin^2 66° & \tan 135°\\sin^2 66° & \tan 135° & \sin^2 14°\\tan 135° & \sin^2 14° & \sin^2 66°\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.note: With a=sin$^2$14°, b=sin$^2$66°, c=tan135°=-1, the determinant equals -(a+b+c)(a$^2$+b$^2$+c$^2$-ab-bc-ca), which is exactly 0 only if a+b+c=0, i.e. sin$^2$14°+sin$^2$66°=1. That identity actually holds for complementary angles summing to 90° (e.g. 24°+66°), not 14°+66°=80°; numerically the determinant with the printed 14° is $\approx$0.27, matching no option. This looks like a printing error for 24° (which would make the identity exact and give 0); KEA's key credits 0.
questions.explanation: Writing a=sin$^2$14°, b=sin$^2$66°, c=tan135°=-1, the determinant equals $3abc-(a^3+b^3+c^3)=-(a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca)$. KEA's key credits 0 (see note on the angle values).

questions.q: The degree measure of $\dfrac{\pi}{32}$ is equal to
The value of sin $\dfrac{5\pi}{12}$ sin $\dfrac{\pi}{12}$ is
questions.explanation: $\sin A\sin B=\frac12[\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)]=\frac12[\cos(\pi/3)-\cos(\pi/2)]=\frac12\left[\frac12-0\right]=\frac14$.

questions.q: $\sqrt{2+\sqrt{2+\sqrt{2+2\cos 8\theta}}}$ =
questions.explanation: Using $2+2\cos X=4\cos^2(X/2)$ repeatedly (with X=8\theta, then 4\theta, then 2\theta) reduces the nested radical to $2\cos\theta$.

questions.q: The trigonometric function y = tan x in the II quadrant
questions.explanation: For $x\in(\pi/2,\pi)$, tan x rises from $-\infty$ (just past $\pi/2$) to 0 (at $\pi$), i.e. it increases from $-\infty$ to 0.

questions.q: The value of cos1200$^\circ$ + tan1485$^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: cos1200$^\circ$ = cos120$^\circ$ = $-1/2$ and tan1485$^\circ$ = tan45$^\circ$ = 1, so the sum is 1/2.

questions.q: The value of tan1$^\circ$ tan2$^\circ$ tan3$^\circ$ ............. tan89$^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: Pairing tan$k^\circ$ with tan(90$-k$)$^\circ$ gives products of 1 for k=1..44, and tan45$^\circ$=1, so the product is 1.

questions.q: The value of $\sin^2 51^\circ+\sin^2 39^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: Since $39^\circ=90^\circ-51^\circ$, $\sin39^\circ=\cos51^\circ$, so the sum is $\sin^2 51^\circ+\cos^2 51^\circ=1$.

questions.q: If $\tan A+\cot A=2$, then the value of $\tan^4 A+\cot^4 A=$
questions.explanation: $\tan A+\cot A=2$ forces $\tan A=\cot A=1$, so $\tan^4A+\cot^4A=1+1=2$.

questions.q: If $\cos x = |\sin x|$ then the general solution is
questions.explanation: $\cos x=|\sin x|$ additionally requires $\cos x\ge0$; solving gives $x=2n\pi\pm\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, which alone keeps $\cos x$ non-negative.

questions.q: $\sqrt{3}\,\text{cosec}\,20^\circ - \sec 20^\circ =$
questions.explanation: Combining over a common denominator, $\sqrt3\cos20^\circ-\sin20^\circ=2\sin40^\circ$ and $\sin20^\circ\cos20^\circ=\tfrac12\sin40^\circ$, giving the value 4.

questions.q: The value of $\cos^2 45^\circ - \sin^2 15^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos^2A-\sin^2B=\cos(A+B)\cos(A-B)=\cos60^\circ\cos30^\circ=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}$.

questions.q: The general solution of $\cot\theta + \tan\theta = 2$ is
questions.explanation: $\cot\theta+\tan\theta=\dfrac{2}{\sin2\theta}=2 \Rightarrow \sin2\theta=1 \Rightarrow 2\theta=n\pi+(-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $\theta=\dfrac{n\pi}{2}+(-1)^n\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.q: If $1 + \sin\theta + \sin^2\theta + \ldots$ upto $\infty = 2\sqrt{3} + 4$, then $\theta =$
questions.explanation: Sum of infinite GP: $\dfrac{1}{1-\sin\theta}=2\sqrt3+4 \Rightarrow \sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\pi/3$.

questions.q: The value of $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\tan(\pi/8)=\sqrt2-1=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2+1}$ after rationalizing.

questions.q: The value of $\sin1° + \sin2° + \ldots + \sin359°$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Terms pair up as $\sin k°+\sin(360-k)°=0$ for $k=1..179$, plus $\sin180°=0$, giving a total of 0.

questions.q: The value of $\tan(1^\circ)+\tan(89^\circ)$ is ____
questions.explanation: $\tan1^\circ+\cot1^\circ=\dfrac{1}{\sin1^\circ\cos1^\circ}=\dfrac{2}{\sin2^\circ}$.

questions.q: If $\sin x+\sin y=\dfrac12$ and $\cos x+\cos y=1$, then $\tan(x+y)=$ ____
questions.explanation: Dividing sum-to-product forms gives $\tan\left(\dfrac{x+y}{2}\right)=\dfrac12$, so $\tan(x+y)=\dfrac{2(1/2)}{1-(1/2)^2}=\dfrac43$.

questions.q: If sin $\theta$ = sin $\alpha$, then
options: $\dfrac{\theta+\alpha}{2}$ is any even multiple of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\theta-\alpha}{2}$ is any odd multiple of $\pi$.
$\dfrac{\theta+\alpha}{2}$ is any multiple of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\theta-\alpha}{2}$ is any even multiple of $\pi$.
$\dfrac{\theta+\alpha}{2}$ is any odd multiple of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\theta-\alpha}{2}$ is any multiple of $\pi$.
$\dfrac{\theta+\alpha}{2}$ is any multiple of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\dfrac{\theta-\alpha}{2}$ is any odd multiple of $\pi$.
questions.explanation: sin$\theta$-sin$\alpha$=$2\cos\left(\frac{\theta+\alpha}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{\theta-\alpha}{2}\right)=0$ gives the two families of solutions in option (3); KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: If tan x = $\dfrac{3}{4}$, $\pi < x < \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, then the value of cos $\dfrac{x}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: In the third quadrant cos x = -4/5. Since x/2 lies in the second quadrant, cos(x/2) is negative: $\cos(x/2)=-\sqrt{(1+\cos x)/2}=-\sqrt{(1/5)/2}=-1/\sqrt{10}$.

questions.q: In a triangle ABC, a|b cos C - c cos B| =
questions.explanation: Using projection formulas $b\cos C = \frac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2a}$ and $c\cos B=\frac{a^2+c^2-b^2}{2a}$, so $a(b\cos C-c\cos B)=b^2-c^2$.

questions.q: $\log(\sin1°)\cdot\log(\sin2°)\cdot\log(\sin3°)\ldots\log(\sin179°)$
questions.explanation: Since $\sin90°=1$, the factor $\log(\sin90°)=0$ makes the whole product zero.

questions.q: If $\sin x-\sin y=\dfrac12$ and $\cos x-\cos y=1$, then $\tan(x+y)=$
questions.explanation: Dividing the sum-to-product forms gives $\cot\dfrac{x+y}{2}=-\dfrac12$, so $\tan(x+y)=\dfrac{2(-2)}{1-4}=\dfrac43$.

questions.q: In a triangle ABC, if $\dfrac{\cos A}{a}=\dfrac{\cos B}{b}=\dfrac{\cos C}{c}$ and $a=2$, then its area is
questions.explanation: The condition forces the triangle to be equilateral, so with side 2 the area is $\sqrt3$.

questions.q: The general solution of $\sin x-\cos x=\sqrt2$, for any integer 'n' is
questions.explanation: $\sqrt2\sin(x-\pi/4)=\sqrt2\Rightarrow\sin(x-\pi/4)=1\Rightarrow x=2n\pi+3\pi/4$.

questions.q: If $\cos\alpha + 2\cos\beta + 3\cos\gamma = 0$, $\sin\alpha + 2\sin\beta + 3\sin\gamma = 0$ and $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = \pi$, then $\sin3\alpha + 8\sin3\beta + 27\sin3\gamma =$
questions.explanation: For $a\cos\alpha+b\cos\beta+c\cos\gamma=0$ and $a\sin\alpha+b\sin\beta+c\sin\gamma=0$ with $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=\pi$, we have $a^3\sin3\alpha+b^3\sin3\beta+c^3\sin3\gamma=3abc\sin(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$. Here $a{=}1,b{=}2,c{=}3$, so the value is $3(1)(2)(3)\sin\pi=0$.

questions.q: $\dfrac{\sin70^\circ + \cos40^\circ}{\cos70^\circ + \sin40^\circ} =$
questions.explanation: $\cos40^\circ=\sin50^\circ$ and $\sin40^\circ=\cos50^\circ$; using sum-to-product, the ratio simplifies to $\dfrac{2\sin60^\circ\cos10^\circ}{2\cos60^\circ\cos10^\circ}=\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$.

questions.q: If $\sin2x = 4\cos x$, then $x =$
questions.explanation: $2\sin x\cos x=4\cos x \Rightarrow \cos x(2\sin x-4)=0$. Since $\sin x=2$ is impossible, $\cos x=0$, whose general solution is $x=2n\pi\pm\pi/2$.

questions.q: In any triangle $ABC$, the simplified form of $\dfrac{\cos 2A}{a^2}-\dfrac{\cos 2B}{b^2}$ is ............
questions.explanation: Using $a=2R\sin A$, $\dfrac{\cos 2A}{a^2}=\dfrac{1-2\sin^2A}{4R^2\sin^2A}=\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{1}{2R^2}$; the $-\dfrac{1}{2R^2}$ terms cancel on subtraction, leaving $\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{1}{b^2}$.

questions.q: The value of $\sin10\cdot\sin30\cdot\sin50\cdot\sin70$ is ............
questions.explanation: Using $\sin\theta\sin(60-\theta)\sin(60+\theta)=\dfrac14\sin3\theta$ with $\theta=10$: $\sin10\sin50\sin70=\dfrac14\sin30=\dfrac18$. Multiplying by $\sin30=\dfrac12$ gives $\dfrac{1}{16}$.

questions.q: A value of $\theta$ satisfying $\sin5\theta-\sin3\theta+\sin\theta=0$ such that $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is ............
questions.explanation: $\sin5\theta+\sin\theta=2\sin3\theta\cos2\theta$, so the equation becomes $\sin3\theta(2\cos2\theta-1)=0$. Taking $\cos2\theta=\dfrac12$ gives $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, which lies in the given range.

questions.q: $\cot12^\circ\cot102^\circ+\cot102^\circ\cot66^\circ+\cot66^\circ\cot12^\circ=$
questions.explanation: Since $12^\circ+102^\circ+66^\circ=180^\circ$, the identity $\cot A\cot B+\cot B\cot C+\cot C\cot A=1$ (for $A+B+C=180^\circ$) gives the value $1$.

questions.q: $(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)(\tan\theta+\cot\theta)=$
questions.explanation: $\tan\theta+\cot\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$, so the product is $\dfrac{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=\sec\theta+\text{cosec}\,\theta$.

questions.q: The sides of a triangle are $6+\sqrt{12}$, $\sqrt{48}$ and $\sqrt{24}$. The tangent of the smallest angle of the triangle is
questions.explanation: The smallest side is $\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt6$; using the cosine rule for the angle opposite it gives $\cos C=\sqrt3/2$, so $C=30^\circ$ and $\tan C=1/\sqrt3$.

questions.q: The general solution of $1+\sin^2x=3\sin x\cdot\cos x$, $\tan x\ne\dfrac{1}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Dividing by $\cos^2x$ gives $2\tan^2x-3\tan x+1=0$, i.e. $\tan x=1/2$ or $1$; excluding $1/2$, $\tan x=1$ gives $x=n\pi+\pi/4$.

questions.q: If $1 + \sin x + \sin^2 x + \ldots$ up to $\infty = 4 + 2\sqrt3$, $0 < x < \pi$ and $x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then $x =$
questions.explanation: The sum of the infinite G.P. is $\dfrac{1}{1-\sin x} = 4+2\sqrt3$, giving $\sin x = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, so $x = \pi/3$ or $2\pi/3$.

questions.q: Which one of the following is possible?
questions.explanation: $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ must lie in $[-1,1]$ and $|\sec\theta|\ge1$, ruling out (1),(2),(3); but $\tan\theta$ can be any real number, so $\tan\theta=45$ is possible.

questions.q: $3(\sin x - \cos x)^4 + 6(\sin x + \cos x)^2 + 4(\sin^6 x + \cos^6 x) =$
questions.explanation: Using $(\sin x-\cos x)^2=1-\sin2x$, $(\sin x+\cos x)^2=1+\sin2x$ and $\sin^6x+\cos^6x=1-\tfrac34\sin^2 2x$, the expression simplifies (all $\sin2x$ terms cancel) to $3+6+4=13$.

questions.q: A cow is tied to a post by a rope. The cow moves along the circular path always keeping the rope tight. If it describes 44 metres, when it has traced out $72^\circ$ at the centre, the length of the rope is
questions.explanation: Arc length $= r\theta$ with $\theta = 72^\circ = \dfrac{2\pi}{5}$ radians, so $r = \dfrac{44}{2\pi/5} = \dfrac{220}{2\pi} \approx 35$ metres (using $\pi=22/7$).
